title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was shot and killed in an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire, early Tuesday morning.
The robbery involved a man and woman luring a victim outside with a firearm on Laurel Hill Road, then fleeing north.
Hollis Police are reviewing footage from local security cameras for evidence and advise no immediate threat to the public.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Former Red Sox infielder Vaughn Grissom criticized the team's analytics-focused approach, attributing his struggles to lack of belief from the organization.
Grissom, now with the Angels, believes his performance improved due to organizational support rather than changes in his play style.
Boston's reliance on data and analytics has faced critique before, with Grissom voicing concern over the balance with observational scouting.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Four family members were shot in a Whitefield, N.H. home, with authorities investigating the case as potential attempted murders and a suicide.
Eric Blake Jr., 29, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound; Amy Blake, 59, and Michael Marro, 41, are critically injured.
Eric Blake Sr., 53, reported the incident after driving himself to a hospital with a gunshot wound and is in stable condition.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial highlights her psychiatric treatment, with testimony about potential bipolar disorder and medication issues.
Massachusetts State Police Sgt. Lawlor testifies on Clancy's use of a psychologist's cellphone to contact her husband from hospital.
Prosecutors argue Clancy deliberately killed her children, while the defense cites postpartum mental illness as an insanity defense.

title: Acton teen located after police discover two dead in home
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Authorities found a woman and teenage boy dead in a home on Martha Lane, Acton.
A 17-year-old resident, Arjun Aravind, was located; no public safety risk reported.
A missing 2014 green Honda Accord linked to the case was found in Wayland.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Corean Reynolds, Boston's nightlife czar, discusses the city's successful summer engaging in large events like FIFA and Boston 250.
The city tested extended hours and outdoor drinking areas, increasing bar and restaurant revenues without reported complaints.
Future plans include less restrictive alcohol regulations and better transportation to support Boston's growing nightlife economy.

title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (Aug. 12)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: A condo in Boston's prestigious Beacon Street sold for a notable $18 million, highest among recent sales.
In Acton, a Colonial-style home at 5 Westside Drive sold for $925,000, built in 2000 with three bedrooms.
Belmont witnessed the sale of a Colonial home at 248 Slade St. for $2,000,000, featuring nine rooms and four bedrooms.

title: Nearly 50 children recovered during anti-human trafficking operation in Greater Boston during the World Cup, officials say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Operation Yellow Card recovered 48 missing children in Massachusetts during the World Cup, targeting human trafficking.
The children, aged 12 to 17, were reunited with families or placed in appropriate services, officials announced.
The operation involved U.S. Marshals, Massachusetts State Police, and Boston Police to combat exploitation and trafficking.

title: Why Patriots rookie Caleb Lomu isn’t fretting over up-and-down training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Patriots rookie Caleb Lomu is focusing on learning from challenges faced during training camp.
Lomu, drafted 28th overall, rotates between left and right tackle, filling in for veteran Morgan Moses.
Veteran Morgan Moses advises Lomu to focus on small daily improvements to avoid being overwhelmed.

title: 12-year-old seriously injured after train surfing Red Line, Transit Police says
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A 12-year-old suffered serious head injuries after falling from a Red Line train while attempting to train surf.
The incident occurred near JFK/UMass station in Dorchester shortly before 1 a.m., according to Transit Police.
Train surfing is a known dangerous activity, with previous incidents involving the Orange Line and a viral video in 2023.
